question.problem:
Consider two sets of $14$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{14},$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{14}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\sum }_{i=1}^{14}{x}_{i}=157, \\  & {\sum }_{i=1}^{14}{y}_{i}=182, \\  & {\sum }_{i=1}^{14}{x}_{i}{y}_{i}=2\,227.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, ${S}_{xy}=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the statistic ${S}_{xy}$ be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}{y}_{i}-\frac{1}{n}({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given statistics in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & =2\,227-\frac{1}{14}(157)(182) \\  & =2\,227-2\,041 \\  & =186.\end{aligned}
$$
